transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Ryland Barton.
President Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance are hitting the campaign trail to try and
boost Republican enthusiasm ahead of the midterm elections.
Vance was in Florida promoting Republican candidate for governor Byron Donalds and Senator
Ashley Moody.
He said Democratic Senate candidate Angie Nixon should leave the country.
When Angie Nixon calls herself a socialist, I think the right response is to say, "Then
get the hell out of here.
You don't belong in America, if those are your views."
Trump is traveling to Texas and Oklahoma, as polls show him losing support from key
groups he made inroads with, like Latinos.
Trump has blamed poor public relations for the party's challenges.
Democrats say Trump and Vance are desperate to rally their base as the elections approach.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says the co-pilot accused of sabotaging a Dubai
to Tel Aviv flight is from Oman, and PR's Count Lonsdorf says that's raising questions
about the pilot vetting process.
Israel does not allow pilots from countries it doesn't have diplomatic relations with
to fly into its airspace.
That includes Oman.
Speaking on Fox News, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Israel checks
the background of pilots flying routes into the country.
He said that this pilot must have gotten through a "loophole."
Israeli officials have said the incident was an attempted terrorist attack, although the
motive is still unknown.
The United Arab Emirates says it's opened an investigation into what happened on the
flight.
It says it's participating in that.
Both the pilot and the co-pilot are alive and being questioned.
Count Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Renee Good's family has sued the U.S. government and several immigration officials alleging
wrongful death, conspiracy, and other violations in the 37-year-old woman's killing by an immigration
officer during the federal crackdown in Minnesota earlier this year.
The killings of Good and Alex Preti during protests sparked outrage across the country.
At least 10 people have died in encounters with immigration officers during Trump's second
term.
President Trump has taken credit for the sharp drop in egg prices since last year.
NPR's Joe Hernandez reports agriculture experts say much of that decline has to do with avian
flu.
An outbreak of avian flu that started in late 2024 was so severe that it resulted in the
deaths of more than 50 million egg-laying hens in just six months.
The hit to the U.S. poultry supply caused egg prices to rise.
But since then, farms have been able to rebuild their flocks, and they've enhanced their
biosecurity protections with help from the Trump administration.
Poultry industry analysts say those efforts, plus a more recent milder avian flu season,
have caused prices to drop again.
In August, egg prices were down 23 percent year-over-year, yet eggs were an exception.
Overall grocery prices had increased by 2.2 percent.
Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
Major U.S. stock indexes rose slightly today.
The S&P 500 rose nearly two-tenths of a percent.
This is NPR News.
France's prime minister has convened a crisis meeting to address nationwide protests by
high school students.
Students are protesting against under-resourced schools and long hours.
Authorities have made hundreds of arrests and reported many injuries.
Marleff candidate Jean-Luc Malenchand has criticized the government's response as repressive.
Prime Minister Sebastian Le Cornu has asked ministers to cancel trips to focus on handling
the protests.
A new crew is closing in on the International Space Station after launch from Cape Canaveral
Space Force Station in Florida on NASA's Crew-13 mission.
Central Florida Public Media's Brendan Byrne reports.
The crew of four includes two NASA astronauts, one from Canada and a Russian cosmonaut.
They launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket aboard the company's Crew Dragon capsule.
It will take the crew only about eight hours to arrive at the station, the fastest travel
time to the ISS by a SpaceX Crew Dragon capsule.
They'll spend nearly half a year living and working on the station, performing science
experiments from the orbiting lab, some even on themselves.
This crew is replacing four people who have been on the station since February.
They'll make the trip back home early next week, splashing down off the coast of Southern
California.
For NPR News, I'm Brendan Byrne at the Kennedy Space Center.
A wind turbine described by its developer as the world's tallest now rises almost 1,200
feet above eastern Germany, surpassing the height of the Eiffel Tower.
The tower's height is supposed to allow it to harness stronger, more reliable winds.
The prototype reached its full height this week.
I'm Rylan Barton, this is NPR News from Washington.
